sermon.speaker: Guest speaker (Freedom House ministry; name not stated)
sermon.summary: After extended worship, a guest speaker shares his testimony and teaches that the great commission belongs to every believer: don’t bury your talent, serve the least of these, and carry people to Jesus like the paralytic’s friends. An altar call follows.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you; and lo, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

“For the kingdom of heaven is like a man traveling to a far country, who called his own servants and delivered his goods to them. And to one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his own ability; and immediately he went on a journey. Then he who had received the five talents went and traded with them, and made another five talents. And likewise he who had received two gained two more also. But he who had received one went and dug in the ground, and hid his lord’s money. After a long time the lord of those servants came and settled accounts with them. “So he who had received five talents came and brought five other talents, saying, ‘Lord, you delivered to me five talents; look, I have gained five more talents besides them.’ His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant; you were faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’ He also who had received two talents came and said, ‘Lord, you delivered to me two talents; look, I have gained two more talents besides them.’ His lord said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.’ “Then he who had received the one talent came and said, ‘Lord, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you have not sown, and gathering where you have not scattered seed. And I was afraid, and went and hid your talent in the ground. Look, there you have what is yours.’ “But his lord answered and said to him, ‘You wicked and lazy servant, you knew that I reap where I have not sown, and gather where I have not scattered seed. So you ought to have deposited my money with the bankers, and at my coming I would have received back my own with interest. So take the talent from him, and give it to him who has ten talents. ‘For to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have abundance; but from him who does not have, even what he has will be taken away. And cast the unprofitable servant into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

chunks.short_answer: The least of these—whatever you did for them you did for Him; gifts serve others, and the great must be servants.
chunks.text:
Then the righteous will answer him,”Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you or thirsty and give you something to drink? When did we see a stranger and invite you in or need clothing and clothe you? When did we see you sick or in prison or go to visit you?” Then the king will reply, “Truly I tell you, whatever you did for the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.” Now, we all know this verse, right? Never seen it like this. This is where it gets rough. Then he will say to those on his left, “Depart from me. You are cursed into the eternal fire prepared for the Devil and his angels. For when I was hungry, you did nothing to help me. You gave me nothing to eat. When I was thirsty, you gave me nothing to drink.

When I was a stranger, you did not invite me in. I needed clothes and you did not clothe me. I was sick and in prison and you did not look after me. They will answer,”Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or needing clothes or sick or in prison and did not help you?” He will reply, “Truly I tell you, whatever you did not do for the dead, dying world that needs me, there’s my words. Whatever you did not do for the least of these, you did not do for me. Then they will go away to eternal punishment, but the righteous to eternal life. I don’t know if y’all are comprehending what this is saying right here, but the Lord says, “You need to take what I gave you and you need to go produce something with it and help my people.” You know what?

Well, who is his people? You know, we know you have to be adopted into sunship, right? We know that we’re all God’s creation, but we’re not all born his children, right? We understand that, right? You have to become his child, right? First John clearly says, “This is how we know who the children of God are and who the children of the Devil are. Those who do not do what is right is not God’s child.” Right? So clearly we have a responsibility as the church to love, to help, to outreach, to do everything we can. Now, how do we do that? It’s a great question. You see, loving our neighbor, caring for widows and orphans, forgiving, bearing burdens, giving, humility, hospitality, laying down your life, preferring others above yourself, all of these things that were things that we should be seeking after.

You know, even the spiritual gifts that’s spoke about in the New Testament are not about the person that has the gift. It’s for the common good of mankind. What about the fruit? Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. Do you know the fruit ain’t for the tree? You know that when you see apples on a tree, is the apples for the tree? No. It’s for everybody else. James 1:27. I hope I’m painting a picture for you now. I hope you get to see it clear religion that God our father accepts as pure and faultless is this to look after orphans and widows in their distress. And let’s don’t forget this part.

And to keep oneself from being polluted by the world or stained by the world. You have got to keep yourself clean while you help other people. You know, people have asked, we’ve had people say to us, “We adopted the first three children. We’ve got two girls at this point, our biological daughters, and we adopted the first three kids, and it was rough, people. I’m just going to be honest with you. We They are still probably the most problematic that we have, okay? But yet, we did it. We fought the fight. We made it through it and then two others come up, you know, and and so on and so forth. But somebody said to us, “Why do y’all keep torturing yourselves? Why are you doing that to yourself?” We’re like, “Why don’t you worry about your business and you let me do what God told me to do, and I’ll let I’ll let him deal with you later, and he can deal with me according to what I did when he told me to.” Amen.

Okay. And so, uh, y’all know why I have authority to preach this message. You know, if you’re not doing something you’re trying to preach, you ain’t got no authority to preach it. Okay? But when you’re walking it out and you’re doing it, there’s a boldness with the authority that the Lord Jesus Christ has given me to speak what I’m speaking to you today because I know it to be true. You see, I I I shared with with with brother Michael, I believe, that after we had been at New Life Church for maybe two years, maybe we’re just bringing people in left and right, and we don’t even realize we’re doing it. Now, did they stay? No. No, they didn’t stay. Many of them didn’t stay. That’s not the point. It’s not my job to make them drink the water. It’s my job to get them to the water. Okay? That’s my job.

It’s my job to present the gospel to you, to present life to you. If you choose it, that’s up to you. But I have a responsibility to get you there or to get it to you, whatever that looks like. And and the pastor’s wife said, “Do y’all mind getting up Sunday and sharing how y’all get so many people to church?” And we looked at each other. “Do we do that? This is just who we became. It came up inside of me. The Lord picked me up out of a pile of garbage and filth and disaster and I need to go tell somebody what he did. It was automatic for me. You know, boy, she mentioned something, too. Woo! I feel my face getting red. When we think about people that don’t know they’re lost, you know, act people like lo act lost.

But, you know, there’s people that are in church. There’s people that have religious experiences that are not surrendered to Jesus. And those are the hardest people on the planet to reach. They might even be living in a nice house and driving a decent car, you know. And I can think of a few people specifically that I have prayed for for years. And one of them finally came and I’m like, “Oh, praise God. Praise God.” But but it’s so hard to break that off of someone that’s living a decent life, the American dream. They’re miserable inside. In Matthew 5:46, these are just quick ones. Surely we know this.

If you love those who love you, what reward will you get? Are not even the tax collectors doing that? You know, some of the most lost people in the world love their children in a worldly love. And if you greet only your own people, what are you doing anymore than others? Don’t even the non-believers do that? And in Luke 6:32, there it is again. If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Big deal. Even sinners love those who love them. In Mark 10 uh 42. Well, they on point, ain’t they? Amen. Jesus called them together and said, “You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the Gentiles Lord it over them and their high officials exercise authority over them.” And he’s speaking to his disciples and he said, “Not so with you.

Instead, whoever wants to be great among you must be your servant.” So all so much for being all prideful. So much for being all about yourself. So much for being full of pride because humble servants can’t be full of pride. All of the sudden you got to have somebody else’s interest above yours. Right? I’m thinking about some verses over there that says love keeps no record of wrongs. Does not seek its own. Come on now. Always about others. Will you put that picture up there for me, please? I want y’all to look close at that.

Don’t say you’re not guilty of this before. So, this man is drowning in his life and his misery. Let me get back in front of this camera. This man is drowning in his life and his misery and a man that should have the answers says, “Dude, just pray about it. It’ll be all right.” No. We ought to reach down and give the man a hand and begin to do whatever the Lord’s called us to do and be the hands and feet of Jesus, right? Is that not what we should do? So your obedience and your surrender and your power to obey was made for this to actually do something. It ain’t just for you.

And you see what begin to happen is we when we begin to love folks, we begin to get in the middle of their mess with them, get down in the in the in the pile of garbage with them and grind with them and and and and get down there and fight with them and love them and help them through things. You know what? All this sudden they said, “Those people over there help you. You need to go see them.” And you know, it became we got this reputation after you helped so many people. Listen, there’s limits. You’ve got to do this by the Holy Spirit. You can’t just give everybody that ask you. It’s got to be led by people that are in that place that they need it. It’s got to be by the Holy Spirit. But that’s where the power is. And then when you become known for that, they won’t call you when they’re all up and high and mighty and high and everything’s going great.
